decisions.question: Endpoint surface — what URL shape should the gateway use for Confluence routes?

options.label: Jira-style verb-noun paths (/api/v1/confluence/page/get, /api/v1/confluence/search, ...); MCP-aligned names live in the sandbox wrapper subcommand layer (Recommended)
Literal MCP-name URL paths (/api/v1/confluence/getConfluencePage, /api/v1/confluence/searchConfluenceUsingCql, ...)
Single endpoint with verb payload field (POST /api/v1/confluence with {verb: ...})
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "Jira-style verb-noun paths (/api/v1/confluence/page/get, /api/v1/confluence/search, ...); MCP-aligned names live in the sandbox wrapper subcommand layer (Recommended)"}

decisions.question: Atlassian API version strategy for v1 of the wrapper?

options.label: v2-first hybrid: v2 for reads + v1 for CQL search + v1 fallback for known v2 comment bugs (Recommended)
v1-only across the board (simpler shape, locks into legacy)
v2-only across the board (CQL search would not be possible without shipping our own search index)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "v2-first hybrid: v2 for reads + v1 for CQL search + v1 fallback for known v2 comment bugs (Recommended)"}

decisions.question: CQL scope extraction — how should we constrain the CQL query surface that the /search endpoint accepts?

options.label: Conservative static space = / space IN (...) extractor; deny-on-ambiguity (mirrors Jira's JQL extractor) (Recommended)
Permissive CQL with post-hoc result filter (rejected for Jira; same risks here)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "Conservative static space = / space IN (...) extractor; deny-on-ambiguity (mirrors Jira's JQL extractor) (Recommended)"}

decisions.question: Comment-quirk handling — how should the wrapper deal with v2 missing nested replies / inline 404s?

options.label: v2-first with transparent v1 fallback for nested replies and inline-404 bugs (Recommended)
v2-only; document the gaps and let agents retry
v1-only for comments; lock in legacy behaviour until Atlassian fixes v2
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "v2-first with transparent v1 fallback for nested replies and inline-404 bugs (Recommended)"}

decisions.question: Default body format for getConfluencePage and related reads?

options.label: Both storage and atlas_doc_format (Recommended — agent gets HTML-ish + ADF in one call)
storage only (smallest payload)
atlas_doc_format only (most structured)
view (rendered HTML) only (lossy on macros / layout)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "Default body-format=storage; support atlas_doc_format and view via caller override. Single body shape on the wire by default to keep payloads small; planners that need ADF tree traversal pass the override per-call."}

decisions.question: Credential sharing between Jira and Confluence?

options.label: Shared ATLASSIAN_BASE_URL / _USERNAME / _API_TOKEN triple, with backward-compat fall-back to JIRA_* and CONFLUENCE_* placeholders (Recommended)
Independent JIRA_* and CONFLUENCE_* triples (status quo of secrets.template.env)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "Shared ATLASSIAN_BASE_URL / _USERNAME / _API_TOKEN triple, with backward-compat fall-back to JIRA_* and CONFLUENCE_* placeholders (Recommended)"}

decisions.question: Network-mode gating shape for /api/v1/confluence/* routes?

options.label: @require_private_mode per route + route-enumeration regression test (Recommended — mirrors Jira)
Move to a Flask blueprint with before_request rejection (would also require migrating Jira; out of scope here)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "@require_private_mode per route + route-enumeration regression test (Recommended — mirrors Jira)"}

decisions.question: Where should the Confluence space allowlist live?

options.label: New confluence.spaces: section in config/context-filters.yaml (Recommended — mirrors Jira's jira.projects)
Dedicated new config/confluence.yaml
CONFLUENCE_SPACE_KEYS env var in secrets.env (placeholder already exists)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "New confluence.spaces: section in config/context-filters.yaml (Recommended — mirrors Jira's jira.projects)"}

decisions.question: Bot identity for Confluence access?

options.label: Same dedicated Atlassian bot account used for Jira (single principal owns both Jira and Confluence read scopes) (Recommended)
Separate bot accounts per service
Reuse the operator's personal Atlassian account
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "Same dedicated Atlassian bot account used for Jira (single principal owns both Jira and Confluence read scopes) (Recommended)"}

decisions.question: Sandbox-visible response redaction stance?

options.label: Strip accountId, emailAddress, and _links.webui user-profile URLs from responses before they reach the sandbox (parallels Jira) (Recommended)
Pass responses through verbatim
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "Strip accountId, emailAddress, and _links.webui user-profile URLs from responses before they reach the sandbox (parallels Jira) (Recommended)"}

decisions.question: getConfluenceSpaces response — should we filter to allowlisted spaces?

options.label: Filter response so only allowlisted spaces are returned (agents cannot enumerate the full tenant space set) (Recommended)
Pass through Atlassian's full space list and rely on per-page allowlist to deny later access
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "Filter response so only allowlisted spaces are returned (agents cannot enumerate the full tenant space set) (Recommended)"}

decisions.question: Attachments endpoints — what is the v1 stance?

options.label: Permanent denylist for v1 and future writes (attachments are arbitrary-file uploads / downloads with unbounded payload surface; if needed later, scope as a separate ticket) (Recommended)
Defer the decision to the future-writes phase
Allow read-only attachment metadata (no body) in v1
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "Permanent denylist for v1 and future writes (attachments are arbitrary-file uploads / downloads with unbounded payload surface; if needed later, scope as a separate ticket) (Recommended)"}

decisions.question: EGG_CONFLUENCE_* environment variables in the sandbox?

options.label: None in v1 (matches issue text — Confluence is reference material, not a unit of work). Audit recovers pageId / spaceKey from each request body (Recommended)
Ship EGG_CONFLUENCE_PAGE / EGG_CONFLUENCE_SPACE as observational env vars (parallel to EGG_JIRA_TICKET)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "None in v1 (matches issue text — Confluence is reference material, not a unit of work). Audit recovers pageId / spaceKey from each request body (Recommended)"}

decisions.question: /execute passthrough endpoint?

options.label: Include it (GET-only, regex-allowlisted), parallel to Jira's escape hatch for read verbs not yet promoted to narrow routes (Recommended)
Skip /execute entirely; add narrow routes only
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "Include it (GET-only, regex-allowlisted), parallel to Jira's escape hatch for read verbs not yet promoted to narrow routes (Recommended)"}

questions.question: Which Atlassian Confluence spaces should be on the v1 allowlist (space keys, comma-separated)?
What is the expected request volume per pipeline (peak CQL searches/min, page reads/min, comment reads/min)? This informs rate-limit defaults and 429 retry behaviour.

Are there custom Confluence fields, macros, or page properties known to hold PII or secrets that should be redacted before sandbox-visible responses (in addition to the accountId / emailAddress defaults)?

For the future write phase (out of scope here), should the gateway enforce idempotency on comment/create (refuse duplicate within N seconds) or leave that to Atlassian's own semantics? Surfacing now so the design-once decision is consistent with Jira.

What pageId / page-link patterns should the orchestrator extract from Jira tickets to feed Confluence reads? (E.g., should it scan ticket descriptions for https://<tenant>.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/<KEY>/pages/<ID>/... and pre-resolve, or leave URL parsing to the agent?) This informs whether v1 needs a page/resolve-by-url verb.
Should getConfluencePageDescendants enforce a maximum depth (e.g., 3) to prevent runaway responses on deeply nested page trees, or pass Atlassian's depth parameter through verbatim?

Should the audit log treat reads of pages whose space is technically in the allowlist but whose page hierarchy is restricted at the Atlassian permission layer as a special audit category (e.g., confluence_upstream_403 separate from confluence_upstream_error)?
For long-lived pages with extensive version history: is there a use case for exposing a version query parameter on getConfluencePage in v1, or should we default to current-version-only?

The host-side mcp__confluence__* MCP authenticates as the consenting human user; the gateway will authenticate as a bot. Are there documents in operator workspaces that the human reads but the bot would not be able to (or vice versa)? If so, do we need a diagnostic command that surfaces the bot's effective access per space?

Should the sandbox confluence wrapper expose MCP-style alias names (confluence get-page, confluence search-cql) in addition to Jira-style subcommands (confluence page get, confluence search), or pick one shape only?
Which Atlassian Confluence spaces should be on the v1 allowlist (space keys, comma-separated)?
questions.answer: Defer to operator at deploy time. Ship with confluence.spaces: [] (empty allowlist, fail-closed) in config/context-filters.yaml; operators populate before enabling Confluence routes. Do not hard-code spaces.

questions.question: What is the expected request volume per pipeline (peak CQL searches/min, page reads/min, comment reads/min)? This informs rate-limit defaults and 429 retry behaviour.
questions.answer: Reuse Jira's rate-limit defaults (single retry on 429 with min(Retry-After, 30); audit confluence_upstream_rate_limited on both attempts). No Confluence-specific tuning in v1; revisit if 429s observed in production.

questions.question: Are there custom Confluence fields, macros, or page properties known to hold PII or secrets that should be redacted before sandbox-visible responses (in addition to the accountId / emailAddress defaults)?
questions.answer: None known; defaults only. Ship with accountId / emailAddress / _links.webui redaction. Add a follow-up ticket if a sensitive macro or page property is identified post-rollout.

questions.question: For the future write phase (out of scope here), should the gateway enforce idempotency on comment/create (refuse duplicate within N seconds) or leave that to Atlassian's own semantics? Surfacing now so the design-once decision is consistent with Jira.
questions.answer: Defer to the future-writes phase; do not pre-design idempotency in v1. Atlassian's create-comment endpoint is not naturally idempotent. Design the idempotency stance at the write-phase ticket alongside Jira's equivalent so the design-once choice stays consistent.

questions.question: What pageId / page-link patterns should the orchestrator extract from Jira tickets to feed Confluence reads? (E.g., should it scan ticket descriptions for https://<tenant>.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/<KEY>/pages/<ID>/... and pre-resolve, or leave URL parsing to the agent?) This informs whether v1 needs a page/resolve-by-url verb.
questions.answer: Do not add a page/resolve-by-url verb in v1. Agents that have a Confluence URL parse the pageId themselves and call /api/v1/confluence/page/get. Add resolve-by-url only if URL-parsing in the agent becomes a recurring pain point; not in v1 scope.

questions.question: Should getConfluencePageDescendants enforce a maximum depth (e.g., 3) to prevent runaway responses on deeply nested page trees, or pass Atlassian's depth parameter through verbatim?
questions.answer: Pass Atlassian's depth parameter through verbatim with no gateway-imposed cap in v1. Add a depth ceiling if a runaway response is observed; not pre-emptively. Document the parameter in the wrapper reference.

questions.question: Should the audit log treat reads of pages whose space is technically in the allowlist but whose page hierarchy is restricted at the Atlassian permission layer as a special audit category (e.g., confluence_upstream_403 separate from confluence_upstream_error)?
questions.answer: Yes, separate confluence_upstream_403 audit category from generic upstream errors. Parallels the not_found vs error split. Helps operators distinguish space-allowlist denials, page-permission denials, and generic upstream errors at audit time.

questions.question: For long-lived pages with extensive version history: is there a use case for exposing a version query parameter on getConfluencePage in v1, or should we default to current-version-only?
questions.answer: Default to current-version only in v1. Do not expose a ?version= query parameter until a use case appears. Document the default in the wrapper reference so future expansion is unsurprising.

questions.question: The host-side mcp__confluence__* MCP authenticates as the consenting human user; the gateway will authenticate as a bot. Are there documents in operator workspaces that the human reads but the bot would not be able to (or vice versa)? If so, do we need a diagnostic command that surfaces the bot's effective access per space?
questions.answer: Operator concern; ship a diagnostic command in a follow-up rather than v1. v1 documents the bot-vs-human access caveat in the wrapper reference. Operators can manually verify the bot's space access at deploy time using the host-side mcp__confluence__* MCP under the bot's token.

questions.question: Should the sandbox confluence wrapper expose MCP-style alias names (confluence get-page, confluence search-cql) in addition to Jira-style subcommands (confluence page get, confluence search), or pick one shape only?
questions.answer: Jira-style subcommands only (e.g., confluence page get, confluence search-cql). Mirrors the existing jira wrapper shape. Do not ship MCP-style aliases in v1; add only if a real porting pain point appears post-rollout.
